The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.370 of 2022 of Thrikkakara Police Station, Ernakulam,
Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158421655/
1

alleging commission of offences under Sections 323, 354, 376(2)(n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 66(E) of the Information Technology Act, 2002 and Section 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The allegation against the petitioner is that, while the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim was working as a receptionist in an ayurvedic spa being conducted by the petitioner, she was subjected to rape.

It is alleged that the accused had also misappropriated and pledged gold ornaments of the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim and that the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim was also threatened stating that her nude pictures will be circulated.

It is also alleged that the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim being a member of the weaker section of the community, offence under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 was also committed by the petitioner.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the allegations raised against the petitioner are totally false.
It is submitted that the petitioner and the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim were in a live-in relationship and they had lived together in the same room for more than two years.
It is not disputed that the petitioner and the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim were running a business together and there were various financial and other transactions between them.

It is submitted that the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim has executed affidavit dated 19.10.2023 a reading of which will suggest that the relationship between the petitioner and the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim was purely consensual.
It is submitted that the affidavit also discloses that the other offences alleged against the petitioner have also not been committed by the petitioner.

4. The learned Public Prosecutor submits that the statement has been recorded from the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim and the statement states that she stands by the averments contained in Annexure-R2(a) affidavit filed in this Court along with Crl.M.A.No.1 of 2023.
5.

The learned counsel appearing for the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim would also submit that the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim stands by the contents of Annexure-R2(a) affidavit and therefore, she does not wish to prosecute the complaint against the petitioner in any manner.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent/defacto complainant/victim and keeping in mind the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Dr.Dhruvaram Muralidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra And Others; [(2019) 18 Supreme Court Cases 191] and Pramod Suryabhan Pawar v.
State of Maharashtra And Another; [(2019) 9 Supreme Court Cases 608], I am of the view that the proceedings against the petitioner can be quashed as it cannot be said that the petitioner has committed any of the offences alleged against the petitioner.
